diagnostic_item.stem: This rectangle is cut into 4 equal parts and 3 are shaded. What fraction of the rectangle is shaded?

intervention.script: Let's shade ONE shape and count: how many parts did we shade out of how many total? That's our one fraction.

learner_evidence.explanation: it's 3/4 because I shaded 3 parts and there are 4 parts total, it's one amount not two numbers

caveats: transfer confirmed on a number line only; set-model transfer not yet attempted
mastery_outcome.claim: Ava can identify a fraction as one quantity, not two separate numbers

misconception.citation: Early rational-number concept development literature on the part-whole construct (Behr, Post & Lesh).
misconception.cognitive_origin: Whole-number-count bias: before a part-whole scheme develops, children read '3/4' as two independent counts read top-to-bottom ('a three and a four') rather than a single quantity describing parts out of a whole.
sprout_forbidden: stating the fraction names one quantity before resolution
misconception.title: A fraction is two separate whole numbers, not one quantity

skill.title: Identify a fraction as a part of a whole
